title: Global Logistics Inventory Visibility
business: A global logistics provider managing millions of shipping containers across thousands of international ports.
problem: The company struggles with fragmented data silos, where tracking information for containers is stored in disparate legacy databases, leading to high latency when generating real-time inventory reports for regional managers.
solution: Elasticsearch acts as a centralized, distributed search and analytics engine that ingests container status updates from various sources into a unified index, allowing for near real-time querying and complex aggregations across the entire global fleet.
steps: Define a consistent index mapping to normalize container status fields across different regional data sources.
Configure ingest pipelines to transform and enrich raw incoming container telemetry data before indexing.
Utilize data streams to manage time-series container tracking events for efficient storage and lifecycle management.
Implement Query DSL to execute complex filtering and aggregation requests for regional inventory dashboards.
Monitor cluster health and shard distribution to ensure high availability and consistent search performance.
outcome: Regional managers gain immediate, unified visibility into container locations and statuses, significantly reducing the time required to generate operational reports.
limitation: A critical limitation is the potential for shard imbalance during heavy ingestion spikes, which can lead to uneven resource utilization across nodes; this is checked by monitoring node-level heap usage and shard distribution statistics.

questions.question: In Global Logistics Inventory Visibility, how does the technology resolve the problem of data silos?
options: By acting as a centralized, distributed search and analytics engine that ingests data into a unified index.
By replacing all legacy databases with a single relational database management system.
By automatically deleting old container data to save storage space.
By forcing all regional managers to use a single manual spreadsheet.
